title: People you may know for user 1
context: Rank second-degree connections by number of mutual friends.
task: Return candidate_id and mutuals for users who are not user 1 and not friends with user 1, ordered by mutuals desc then candidate_id, top 5.
hint: Edges CTE; friends of my friends grouped by candidate, exclude direct friends.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships), f1 AS (SELECT v FROM e WHERE u = 1) SELECT e.v AS candidate_id, COUNT(*) AS mutuals FROM e JOIN f1 ON f1.v = e.u WHERE e.v <> 1 AND e.v NOT IN (SELECT v FROM f1) GROUP BY e.v ORDER BY mutuals DESC, candidate_id LIMIT 5;

title: Mutual-friend count for every friendship
context: The number shown on each friend's profile.
task: Return user_a, user_b and mutuals = number of users friends with both, for friendships with at least 2 mutuals.
hint: Edges CTE joined twice on a common neighbour.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships) SELECT f.user_a, f.user_b, COUNT(*) AS mutuals FROM friendships f JOIN e a ON a.u = f.user_a JOIN e b ON b.u = f.user_b AND b.v = a.v GROUP BY f.friendship_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

title: Count triangles
context: Closed triads (A–B, B–C, A–C) indicate tight communities.
task: Return triangles = number of user triples that are all mutually friends (each triangle counted once).
hint: Join friendships three times with a < b < c.
answer: SELECT COUNT(*) AS triangles FROM friendships ab JOIN friendships bc ON bc.user_a = ab.user_b JOIN friendships ac ON ac.user_a = ab.user_a AND ac.user_b = bc.user_b;

title: Clustering coefficient per user
context: Of a user's friend pairs, what share are themselves friends?
task: Return user_id, friends and clustering_pct (1 dp) = connected friend pairs / (friends × (friends − 1) / 2) × 100, for users with 3+ friends.
hint: Edges CTE; count pairs (x<y) among neighbours that are in friendships.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships), n AS (SELECT u, COUNT(*) AS friends FROM e GROUP BY u HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3), pairs AS (SELECT a.u, COUNT(*) AS linked FROM e a JOIN e b ON b.u = a.u AND b.v > a.v JOIN friendships f ON f.user_a = a.v AND f.user_b = b.v GROUP BY a.u) SELECT n.u AS user_id, n.friends, ROUND(COALESCE(pairs.linked, 0) * 100.0 / (n.friends * (n.friends - 1) / 2.0), 1) AS clustering_pct FROM n LEFT JOIN pairs ON pairs.u = n.u;

title: Shortest path length from user 1 (up to 3 hops)
context: Degrees of separation.
task: Using a recursive CTE, return user_id and hops = minimum number of hops from user 1, for users reachable within 3 hops (excluding user 1).
hint: Recursive frontier with depth; take MIN(depth) per user.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships), bfs(user_id, hops) AS (SELECT v, 1 FROM e WHERE u = 1 UNION ALL SELECT e.v, bfs.hops + 1 FROM bfs JOIN e ON e.u = bfs.user_id WHERE bfs.hops < 3) SELECT user_id, MIN(hops) AS hops FROM bfs WHERE user_id <> 1 GROUP BY user_id;

title: Users reachable within 2 hops, per user
context: Network reach size.
task: Return user_id and reach2 = number of distinct users within 2 hops (excluding self), for users with at least one friend.
hint: Edges CTE; union of 1-hop and 2-hop neighbours, DISTINCT.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships), r AS (SELECT u AS user_id, v AS other FROM e UNION SELECT a.u, b.v FROM e a JOIN e b ON b.u = a.v WHERE b.v <> a.u) SELECT user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT other) AS reach2 FROM r GROUP BY user_id;

title: Are users 1 and 30 connected?
context: Same community or separate islands?
task: Return connected = 1 if user 30 is reachable from user 1 within 6 hops, else 0 (single row).
hint: Recursive BFS with a visited guard via depth limit; EXISTS.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships), bfs(user_id, hops) AS (SELECT 1, 0 UNION ALL SELECT e.v, bfs.hops + 1 FROM bfs JOIN e ON e.u = bfs.user_id WHERE bfs.hops < 6) SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bfs WHERE user_id = 30) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS connected;

title: Degree distribution
context: How many users have 1 friend, 2 friends, …?
task: Return friends (degree) and users = number of users with that degree, ordered by friends.
hint: Degree CTE, then GROUP BY degree.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS friends FROM (SELECT user_a AS user_id FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b FROM friendships) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT friends, COUNT(*) AS users FROM d GROUP BY friends ORDER BY friends;

title: Friends' total reach
context: A proxy for network influence: sum of reach of posts by your friends.
task: Return user_id and friends_reach = SUM(reach) of posts authored by the user's friends, top 5 by friends_reach (ties by user_id).
hint: Edges CTE joined to a per-user reach CTE.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships), r AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(reach) AS reach FROM posts GROUP BY user_id) SELECT e.u AS user_id, SUM(r.reach) AS friends_reach FROM e JOIN r ON r.user_id = e.v GROUP BY e.u ORDER BY friends_reach DESC, user_id LIMIT 5;

title: Top post per user by engagement
context: Each creator's best-performing post.
task: Return user_id, post_id and engagement_pct (2 dp) for the post with the highest (likes+comments+shares)/reach per user (ties by post_id).
hint: ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY user_id.
answer: SELECT user_id, post_id, ROUND(eng * 100, 2) AS engagement_pct FROM (SELECT user_id, post_id, (likes + comments + shares) * 1.0 / reach AS eng, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY (likes + comments + shares) * 1.0 / reach DESC, post_id) AS rn FROM posts) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Top 3 posts per platform by reach
context: Platform leaderboards.
task: Return platform, post_id and reach for the top 3 by reach per platform (DENSE_RANK, ties included).
hint: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY platform ORDER BY reach DESC).
answer: SELECT platform, post_id, reach FROM (SELECT platform, post_id, reach, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY platform ORDER BY reach DESC) AS rk FROM posts) WHERE rk <= 3;

title: Cumulative friendships over time
context: Network size growth curve by month.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM), new_edges and cumulative_edges ordered by month.
hint: SUM() OVER (ORDER BY month).
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', created_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS new_edges FROM friendships GROUP BY month) SELECT month, new_edges, SUM(new_edges) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS cumulative_edges FROM m;

title: Post-over-post like change per user
context: Is each user's engagement trending up?
task: Return user_id, post_id and like_change = likes − previous post's likes (by post_date, post_id), only where a previous post exists.
hint: LAG(likes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY post_date, post_id).
answer: SELECT user_id, post_id, like_change FROM (SELECT user_id, post_id, likes - LAG(likes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY post_date, post_id) AS like_change FROM posts) WHERE like_change IS NOT NULL;

title: Creator tiers by total reach
context: Bronze/Silver/Gold from reach quartiles… as 4 tiers.
task: Return user_id, total_reach and tier = NTILE(4) ordered by total_reach descending (1 = top) for users with posts.
hint: CTE then NTILE.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(reach) AS total_reach FROM posts GROUP BY user_id) SELECT user_id, total_reach, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_reach DESC) AS tier FROM t;

title: User share of country reach
context: Who dominates each market's distribution?
task: Return country, user_id and pct_of_country (1 dp) = user reach / country reach * 100, for users with posts.
hint: SUM OVER (PARTITION BY country).
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT u.country, p.user_id, SUM(p.reach) AS reach FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY p.user_id) SELECT country, user_id, ROUND(reach * 100.0 / SUM(reach) OVER (PARTITION BY country), 1) AS pct_of_country FROM r;

title: Rolling 3-post average likes
context: Smoothed performance per user.
task: Return user_id, post_id, likes and ma3 (1 dp) = average likes over the current and 2 preceding posts of that user (by post_date, post_id).
hint: AVG OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ... ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
answer: SELECT user_id, post_id, likes, ROUND(AVG(likes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY post_date, post_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 1) AS ma3 FROM posts;

title: Posting retention by signup year
context: Share of each signup cohort that has posted in 2025.
task: Return signup_year and active_2025_pct (1 dp) = users with a post dated in 2025 / users in the cohort * 100.
hint: EXISTS with a year filter inside AVG(CASE).
answer: SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', u.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS signup_year, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM posts p WHERE p.user_id = u.user_id AND p.post_date >= '2025-01-01') THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS active_2025_pct FROM users u GROUP BY signup_year;

title: Friends made in the first 30 days
context: Early social connection predicts retention.
task: Return user_id and early_friends = friendships created within 30 days of the user's signup (either side), for users with early_friends > 0.
hint: Edges CTE joined to users with a julianday window.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, created_at FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, created_at FROM friendships) SELECT u.user_id, COUNT(*) AS early_friends FROM users u JOIN e ON e.u = u.user_id AND julianday(e.created_at) - julianday(u.signup_date) BETWEEN 0 AND 30 GROUP BY u.user_id;

title: Longest daily posting streak
context: Consecutive days with a post, per user.
task: Return user_id and longest_streak, for users whose longest streak is 2 or more.
hint: Distinct dates per user, ROW_NUMBER, date(d, -rn days).
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, post_date FROM posts), g AS (SELECT user_id, post_date, date(post_date, '-' || ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY post_date) || ' days') AS grp FROM d), s AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS streak FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp) SELECT user_id, MAX(streak) AS longest_streak FROM s GROUP BY user_id HAVING MAX(streak) >= 2;

title: Median reach per platform
context: Reach is heavy-tailed; the median tells the truth.
task: Return platform and median_reach (1 dp).
hint: ROW_NUMBER/COUNT partitioned by platform.
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT platform, reach, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY platform ORDER BY reach) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY platform) AS cnt FROM posts) SELECT platform, ROUND(AVG(reach), 1) AS median_reach FROM r WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2) GROUP BY platform;

title: Top 5% posts by reach
context: Breakout content.
task: Return post_id and reach where PERCENT_RANK over reach >= 0.95.
hint: PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY reach).
answer: SELECT post_id, reach FROM (SELECT post_id, reach, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY reach) AS pr FROM posts) WHERE pr >= 0.95;

title: Users generating 80% of reach
context: How concentrated is distribution?
task: Return user_id and total_reach for users whose cumulative reach (desc, ties by user_id) reaches 80% of total — include the one crossing 80%.
hint: Running SUM with 1 PRECEDING vs 0.8 × total.
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(reach) AS total_reach FROM posts GROUP BY user_id), c AS (SELECT user_id, total_reach, SUM(total_reach) OVER (ORDER BY total_reach DESC, user_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_cum, SUM(total_reach) OVER () AS total FROM r) SELECT user_id, total_reach FROM c WHERE COALESCE(prev_cum, 0) < 0.8 * total;

title: Reactions by type per platform
context: Wide table: like/love/haha/wow/sad/angry columns.
task: Return platform and one column per reaction type with counts.
hint: Join posts; conditional SUM ×6.
answer: SELECT p.platform, SUM(CASE WHEN r.reaction = 'like' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS like_n, SUM(CASE WHEN r.reaction = 'love' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS love_n, SUM(CASE WHEN r.reaction = 'haha' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS haha_n, SUM(CASE WHEN r.reaction = 'wow' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wow_n, SUM(CASE WHEN r.reaction = 'sad' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sad_n, SUM(CASE WHEN r.reaction = 'angry' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS angry_n FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id GROUP BY p.platform;

title: Posts per week including empty weeks
context: Weekly content chart for 2025 H1.
task: Return week_start (Mondays from '2025-01-06' to '2025-06-30') and posts in [week_start, week_start+6], ordered.
hint: Recursive 7-day series + LEFT JOIN range.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE w(week_start) AS (SELECT '2025-01-06' UNION ALL SELECT date(week_start, '+7 days') FROM w WHERE week_start < '2025-06-30') SELECT w.week_start, COUNT(p.post_id) AS posts FROM w LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.post_date >= w.week_start AND p.post_date <= date(w.week_start, '+6 days') GROUP BY w.week_start ORDER BY w.week_start;

title: Second most-liked post per platform
context: Runner-up content.
task: Return platform, post_id and likes for DENSE_RANK = 2 by likes within platform.
hint: DENSE_RANK per platform.
answer: SELECT platform, post_id, likes FROM (SELECT platform, post_id, likes, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY platform ORDER BY likes DESC) AS rk FROM posts) WHERE rk = 2;

title: ROAS-style efficiency ranking
context: Rank campaigns by conversions per 1,000 impressions within platform.
task: Return platform, advertiser, conv_per_k (2 dp) = conversions * 1000.0 / impressions and rk = RANK() by conv_per_k desc within platform.
hint: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY platform ...).
answer: SELECT platform, advertiser, ROUND(conversions * 1000.0 / impressions, 2) AS conv_per_k, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY platform ORDER BY conversions * 1000.0 / impressions DESC) AS rk FROM ad_campaigns;

title: Spend share vs conversion share
context: Campaigns that get a bigger share of conversions than of spend are efficient.
task: Return advertiser, spend_share_pct (1 dp), conv_share_pct (1 dp) and efficient = 1 if conv share > spend share else 0.
hint: SUM() OVER () for totals.
answer: SELECT advertiser, ROUND(spend * 100.0 / SUM(spend) OVER (), 1) AS spend_share_pct, ROUND(conversions * 100.0 / SUM(conversions) OVER (), 1) AS conv_share_pct, CASE WHEN conversions * 1.0 / SUM(conversions) OVER () > spend * 1.0 / SUM(spend) OVER () THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS efficient FROM ad_campaigns;

title: Users who reacted to every viral post
context: Superfans of breakout content (reach > 10000).
task: Return user_id for users who have a reaction on every post with reach > 10000.
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT post) among viral = total viral posts.
answer: SELECT r.user_id FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id WHERE p.reach > 10000 GROUP BY r.user_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.post_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE reach > 10000);

title: Friends, posts and reactions per user without fan-out
context: Three one-to-many facts per user in one row.
task: Return user_id, friends, posts, reactions_given for every user (0s where none).
hint: Three CTEs, LEFT JOIN from users.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS friends FROM (SELECT user_a AS user_id FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b FROM friendships) GROUP BY user_id), p AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS posts FROM posts GROUP BY user_id), r AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS reactions_given FROM reactions GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.user_id, COALESCE(d.friends, 0) AS friends, COALESCE(p.posts, 0) AS posts, COALESCE(r.reactions_given, 0) AS reactions_given FROM users u LEFT JOIN d ON d.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN p ON p.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN r ON r.user_id = u.user_id;

title: Do friends share a country more than chance?
context: Compare observed same-country share with the share expected from the country mix.
task: Return observed_pct (1 dp) = same-country friendships share, and expected_pct (1 dp) = Σ over countries of (users_c / total)² × 100.
hint: Two scalar subqueries; expected uses a GROUP BY country subquery.
answer: SELECT (SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN a.country = b.country THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) FROM friendships f JOIN users a ON a.user_id = f.user_a JOIN users b ON b.user_id = f.user_b) AS observed_pct, (SELECT ROUND(SUM(share * share) * 100, 1) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users) AS share FROM users GROUP BY country)) AS expected_pct;

title: Comment-to-like ratio outliers
context: Posts where people argue: comments unusually high vs likes.
task: Return post_id, likes, comments and ratio (2 dp) = comments * 1.0 / likes for posts with likes >= 50 and ratio > 0.25.
hint: Row-level ratio filter.
answer: SELECT post_id, likes, comments, ROUND(comments * 1.0 / likes, 2) AS ratio FROM posts WHERE likes >= 50 AND comments * 1.0 / likes > 0.25;

title: First platform vs main platform
context: Do users stick with the app they started on?
task: Return user_id, first_platform (earliest post) and main_platform (most posts; ties by platform) only where they differ.
hint: FIRST_VALUE + ROW_NUMBER on counts.
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, FIRST_VALUE(platform) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY post_date, post_id) AS first_platform FROM posts), c AS (SELECT user_id, platform, COUNT(*) AS n FROM posts GROUP BY user_id, platform), m AS (SELECT user_id, platform AS main_platform FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY n DESC, platform) AS rn FROM c) WHERE rn = 1) SELECT f.user_id, f.first_platform, m.main_platform FROM f JOIN m ON m.user_id = f.user_id WHERE f.first_platform <> m.main_platform;

title: Friendships that connect different countries' clusters
context: Edges whose two users share no mutual friends — potential bridges.
task: Return user_a and user_b for friendships with zero mutual friends.
hint: NOT EXISTS on a common neighbour via the edges CTE.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships) SELECT f.user_a, f.user_b FROM friendships f WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM e a JOIN e b ON b.v = a.v WHERE a.u = f.user_a AND b.u = f.user_b);
